messages.subject: micro_global vs micro_ncep
parts:
Hi All,

I am playing with the functions micro_ncep and micro_global to obtain microclimates for various locations in South Africa. I compared the results for the same location yearly mean and what I am getting is quite different (I am attaching an example of what I obtained for solar irradiance at 0% shade). From my understanding both are based on the NicheMapR microclimate model and the difference lays in the daily weather database used. So how should I choose between them?
So far the only thing I struggled with is that micro_ncep doesn't allow you to set the soil type (e.g. my animals are standing on rocks even if the substrate around is sand. So I guess soilgrid would count the substrate as "sand" but that wouldn't be relevant in my case) making me leaning towards micro_global.
What are your opinions?

Fede

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: micro_global vs micro_ncep
parts:
Hi there Fede,

Are you using the most recent version of NicheMapR? There were some issues with an earlier version of microclima in the way it feed into the micro_ncep function as well as a few other things that got straightened out. Note that the micro_ncep function uses the NCEP solar radiation (6-hourly interpolated to hourly) whereas the micro_global computes it from first principles and the given cloud cover.

More generally, the micro_global function is using a monthly long-term average climatology (1960-1990) while the micro_ncep allows you to use historical forcing data. Which is the more suitable dataset depends very much on what question you're trying to answer.

All the best,
Mike
